publication_scope.blurb: Ludwig Crocius — Book I Chapter 4 On the affections of Sacred Scripture, specifically its AUTHORITY, from the 1636 Bremen Latin. Densify COMPLETE (PHYS 177-210 Cap.4 close): affections; self-attesting authority; absolute vs comparative; against papal suspension; human occasions/inclinations; Spirit's divine argument through Aph. XV; how the church today knows the Word; four conclusions on clear dogma, traditional consensus, uncertain additions, and useful non-necessary doctrine; Cap. 4 close against false prophets and additions. Cap. 5 On perfection and sufficiency begins PHYS 210; the rest of the Syntagma remains.
publication_scope.era_note: Crocius wrote in the early seventeenth century as Reformed professor at the illustrious school of Bremen. This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. The 1636 Villerian folio is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
publication_scope.first_english_note: No complete public-domain English of this 1636 Latin Syntagma was locked as reading text. This is a new rendering from locked Latin for Liber I Cap. 4 densify complete.

text_history.method: English follows the locked 1636 Bremen Latin of Liber I Cap. 4 densify COMPLETE, reconstructed from SLUB Dresden page images (PHYS 177-210 Cap.4 close). Same-page OCR (tesseract lat + Vision) used as check. No modern English was copied. Cap. 5 (CAPUT QUINTUM / De sacrae Scripturae perfectione & sufficientia) begins PHYS 210. No Internet Archive copy was located.
